claim: Genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk affect gene regulation in metabolically relevant tissues, such as pancreatic islets.
source: Genetic variants associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk affect gene regulation in metabolically relevant tissues, such as pancreatic islets.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that references established knowledge in the field about T2D genetic variants affecting gene regulation in metabolically relevant tissues.

claim: T2D variants are enriched in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers that are not active in islets.
source: Generation of chromatin maps from developmental precursors throughout pancreatic differentiation of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) identifies enrichment of T2D variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers that are not active in islets.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on chromatin mapping and variant enrichment analysis.

claim: Genes associated with progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are predicted to regulate developmental processes, most notably tissue morphogenesis.
source: Genes associated with progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are predicted to regulate developmental processes, most notably tissue morphogenesis.
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of genes near progenitor-specific stretch enhancers.

claim: Progenitor-specific enhancers harboring T2D-associated variants regulate cell polarity genes LAMA1 and CRB2.
source: Through gene editing in hESCs, we demonstrate that progenitor-specific enhancers harboring T2D-associated variants regulate cell polarity genes LAMA1 and CRB2.
evidence: This is demonstrated through CRISPR-mediated deletion experiments in hESCs.

claim: Knockdown of lama1 or crb2 in zebrafish embryos causes a defect in pancreas morphogenesis.
source: Knockdown of lama1 or crb2 in zebrafish embryos causes a defect in pancreas morphogenesis and impairs islet cell development.
evidence: This is based on morpholino knockdown experiments in zebrafish showing annular pancreas phenotype.

claim: Knockdown of lama1 or crb2 in zebrafish embryos impairs islet cell development.
source: Knockdown of lama1 or crb2 in zebrafish embryos causes a defect in pancreas morphogenesis and impairs islet cell development.
evidence: This is based on quantification of beta cell numbers in zebrafish morphants.

claim: A subset of T2D risk variants specifically affects pancreatic developmental programs.
source: Together, our findings reveal that a subset of T2D risk variants specifically affects pancreatic developmental programs, suggesting that dysregulation of developmental processes can predispose to T2D.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the enrichment analysis and functional studies.

claim: Dysregulation of developmental processes can predispose to T2D.
source: Together, our findings reveal that a subset of T2D risk variants specifically affects pancreatic developmental programs, suggesting that dysregulation of developmental processes can predispose to T2D.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings of the study.

claim: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder characterized by insulin insensitivity and insufficient insulin secretion by pancreatic beta cells.
source: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder characterized by insulin insensitivity and insufficient insulin secretion by pancreatic beta cells (Halban et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about T2D supported by citation.

claim: Genetic association studies have identified hundreds of loci influencing risk of T2D.
source: Genetic association studies have identified hundreds of loci influencing risk of T2D (Mahajan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from GWAS studies supported by citation.

claim: The majority of T2D risk variants map to non-coding sequence.
source: The majority of T2D risk variants map to non-coding sequence, suggesting that genetic risk of T2D is largely mediated through variants affecting transcriptional regulatory activity.
evidence: This is established knowledge from genetic studies.

claim: Genetic risk of T2D is largely mediated through variants affecting transcriptional regulatory activity.
source: The majority of T2D risk variants map to non-coding sequence, suggesting that genetic risk of T2D is largely mediated through variants affecting transcriptional regulatory activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most variants are non-coding.

claim: T2D risk variants are enriched in regulatory sites active in pancreatic beta cells.
source: Intersection of T2D risk variants with epigenomic data has uncovered enrichment of T2D risk variants in regulatory sites active in specific cell types, predominantly in pancreatic beta cells, including risk variants that affect regulatory activity directly (Chiou et al., 2019; Fuchsberger et al., 2016; Gaulton et al., 2015; Gaulton et al., 2010; Greenwald et al., 2019; Mahajan et al., 2018; Parker et al., 2013; Pasquali et al., 2014; Thurner et al., 2018; Varshney et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from multiple cited studies.

claim: T2D risk-associated variants are enriched within large, contiguous regions of islet active chromatin, referred to as stretch or super-enhancers.
source: T2D risk-associated variants are further enriched within large, contiguous regions of islet active chromatin, referred to as stretch or super-enhancers (Parker et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited study.

claim: Stretch enhancers preferentially bind islet-cell-restricted transcription factors and drive islet-specific gene expression.
source: These regions of active chromatin preferentially bind islet-cell-restricted transcription factors and drive islet-specific gene expression (Parker et al., 2013; Pasquali et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: Many genes associated with T2D risk in islets are also expressed in pancreatic progenitor cells during embryonic development.
source: Many genes associated with T2D risk in islets are not uniquely expressed in differentiated islet endocrine cells, but also in pancreatic progenitor cells during embryonic development.
evidence: This is an observation based on gene expression patterns.

claim: T2D risk variants map to HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, MNX1, NEUROG3, PAX4, and PDX1.
source: For example, T2D risk variants map to HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, MNX1, NEUROG3, PAX4, and PDX1 (Flannick et al., 2019; Mahajan et al., 2018; Steinthorsdottir et al., 2014), which are all transcription factors also expressed in pancreatic developmental precursors.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited GWAS studies.

claim: HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, MNX1, NEUROG3, PAX4, and PDX1 are transcription factors expressed in pancreatic developmental precursors.
source: For example, T2D risk variants map to HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, MNX1, NEUROG3, PAX4, and PDX1 (Flannick et al., 2019; Mahajan et al., 2018; Steinthorsdottir et al., 2014), which are all transcription factors also expressed in pancreatic developmental precursors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about gene expression patterns.

claim: Inactivation of HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, MNX1, NEUROG3, PAX4, and PDX1 causes defects in endocrine cell development, resulting in reduced beta cell numbers.
source: Studies in model organisms and hESC-based models of pancreatic endocrine cell differentiation have shown that inactivation of these transcription factors causes defects in endocrine cell development, resulting in reduced beta cell numbers (Gaertner et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies in model organisms and hESC models.

claim: Heterozygous mutations for HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, PAX4, and PDX1 are associated with maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY).
source: Furthermore, heterozygous mutations for HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, PAX4, and PDX1 are associated with maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY), which is an autosomal dominant form of diabetes with features similar to T2D (Urakami, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited study.

claim: MODY is an autosomal dominant form of diabetes with features similar to T2D.
source: Furthermore, heterozygous mutations for HNF1A, HNF1B, HNF4A, PAX4, and PDX1 are associated with maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY), which is an autosomal dominant form of diabetes with features similar to T2D (Urakami, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited study.

claim: Disturbed intrauterine metabolic conditions, such as maternal malnutrition, can lead to reduced beta cell mass and T2D predisposition in the offspring.
source: Observations showing that disturbed intrauterine metabolic conditions, such as maternal malnutrition, can lead to reduced beta cell mass and T2D predisposition in the offspring (Lumey et al., 2015; Nielsen et al., 2014; Portha et al., 2011) support the concept that compromised beta cell development could predispose to T2D.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited epidemiological and animal studies.

claim: Compromised beta cell development could predispose to T2D.
source: Observations showing that disturbed intrauterine metabolic conditions, such as maternal malnutrition, can lead to reduced beta cell mass and T2D predisposition in the offspring (Lumey et al., 2015; Nielsen et al., 2014; Portha et al., 2011) support the concept that compromised beta cell development could predispose to T2D.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited observations.

claim: Stretch enhancers comprised 7.7%, 7.8%, 8.8%, 8.1%, 8.1%, and 10.4% of active enhancers in ES, DE, GT, PP1, PP2, and islets, respectively.
source: Consistent with prior observations of SE features (Parker et al., 2013; Whyte et al., 2013), SE comprised a small subset of all active enhancers (7.7%, 7.8%, 8.8%, 8.1%, 8.1%, and 10.4% of active enhancers in ES, DE, GT, PP1, PP2, and islets, respectively; Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the chromatin state analysis shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Genes proximal to stretch enhancers were more highly expressed than genes proximal to typical enhancers.
source: and genes proximal to SE were more highly expressed than genes proximal to TE (p=4.68 × 10−7, 4.64 × 10−11, 1.31 × 10−5, 8.85 × 10−9, 5.34 × 10−6, and <2.2 × 10−16 for expression of genes near TE vs SE in ES, DE, GT, PP1, PP2, and islets, respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Nearly all identified stretch enhancers contained at least one ATAC-seq peak.
source: Nearly all identified SE contained at least one ATAC-seq peak (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is a finding from ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: At the PP2 stage, 62.3% of stretch enhancers harbored one ATAC-seq peak, 32.2% harbored two or three, and 0.7% harbored four or more ATAC-seq peaks.
source: At the PP2 stage, 62.3% of SE harbored one, 32.2% two or three, and 0.7% four or more ATAC-seq peaks (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: T2D-associated variants showed strongest enrichment in islet stretch enhancers (log enrichment = 2.18, 95% CI = 1.80, 2.54).
source: We observed strongest enrichment of T2D-associated variants in islet SE (log enrichment = 2.18, 95% CI = 1.80, 2.54) and late pancreatic progenitor SE (log enrichment = 2.17, 95% CI = 1.40, 2.74)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from functional GWAS enrichment analysis.

claim: T2D-associated variants showed strong enrichment in late pancreatic progenitor stretch enhancers (log enrichment = 2.17, 95% CI = 1.40, 2.74).
source: We observed strongest enrichment of T2D-associated variants in islet SE (log enrichment = 2.18, 95% CI = 1.80, 2.54) and late pancreatic progenitor SE (log enrichment = 2.17, 95% CI = 1.40, 2.74)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from functional GWAS enrichment analysis.

claim: Enrichment of T2D-associated variants was more pronounced when only considering variants in accessible chromatin sites within stretch enhancers (islet log enrichment = 3.20, 95% CI = 2.74, 3.60; PP2 log enrichment = 3.18, 95% CI = 2.35, 3.79).
source: which was more pronounced when only considering variants in accessible chromatin sites within these elements (islet log enrichment = 3.20, 95% CI = 2.74, 3.60; PP2 log enrichment = 3.18, 95% CI = 2.35, 3.79; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from functional GWAS enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Variants in accessible chromatin sites of late pancreatic progenitor stretch enhancers were enriched for T2D association in a joint model including islet stretch enhancers (islet log enrichment = 2.94, 95% CI = 2.47, 3.35; PP2 log enrichment = 1.27, 95% CI = 0.24, 2.00).
source: Variants in accessible chromatin sites of late pancreatic progenitor SE were enriched for T2D association in a joint model including islet SE (islet log enrichment = 2.94, 95% CI = 2.47, 3.35; PP2 log enrichment = 1.27, 95% CI = 0.24, 2.00; Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from joint model analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Enrichment of variants in accessible chromatin sites of pancreatic progenitor stretch enhancers was observed after conditioning on islet stretch enhancers (log enrichment = 0.60, 95% CI = −0.87, 1.48).
source: We also observed enrichment of variants in accessible chromatin sites of pancreatic progenitor SE after conditioning on islet SE (log enrichment = 0.60, 95% CI = −0.87, 1.48)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from conditional analysis.

claim: Enrichment of variants was observed when excluding pancreatic progenitor stretch enhancers active in islets (log enrichment = 1.62, 95% CI = <-20, 3.14).
source: as well as when excluding pancreatic progenitor SE active in islets (log enrichment = 1.62, 95% CI = <-20, 3.14).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from exclusion analysis.

claim: Known T2D loci with T2D-associated variants in stretch enhancers active in pancreatic progenitors but not in islets included LAMA1 and PROX1.
source: Examples of known T2D loci with T2D-associated variants in SE active in pancreatic progenitors but not in islets included LAMA1 and PROX1.
evidence: This is an observation from the variant mapping analysis.

claim: A subset of T2D variants may affect disease risk by altering regulatory programs specifically active in pancreatic progenitors.
source: These results suggest that a subset of T2D variants may affect disease risk by altering regulatory programs specifically active in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment analysis results.

claim: A total of 492 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers were identified genome-wide.
source: Applying these criteria, we identified a total of 492 PSSE genome-wide (Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the chromatin state classification shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers acquired broad deposition of the active enhancer mark H3K27ac at the PP1 and PP2 stages.
source: As expected based on their chromatin state classification, PSSE acquired broad deposition of the active enhancer mark H3K27ac at the PP1 and PP2 stages (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: 93.5% of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers contained at least one accessible chromatin site at the PP2 stage.
source: Coincident with an increase in H3K27ac signal, chromatin accessibility at PSSE also increased (Figure 2B), and 93.5% of PSSE contained at least one accessible chromatin site at the PP2 stage (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: 42%, 48%, 63%, and 17% of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers were poised in ES, DE, GT, and PP1, respectively.
source: Further investigation of PSSE chromatin state dynamics at earlier stages of pancreatic differentiation revealed that PSSE were often poised (defined by H3K4me1 in the absence of H3K27ac) prior to activation (42%, 48%, 63%, and 17% of PSSE in ES, DE, GT, and PP1, respectively; Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from chromatin state analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A poised enhancer state frequently precedes enhancer activation during development.
source: consistent with earlier observations that a poised enhancer state frequently precedes enhancer activation during development (Rada-Iglesias et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: 13%, 23%, 29%, and 46% of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers were classified as typical enhancers in ES, DE, GT, and PP1, respectively.
source: Intriguingly, a subset of PSSE was classified as TE earlier in development (13%, 23%, 29%, and 46% of PSSE in ES, DE, GT, and PP1, respectively; Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from chromatin state analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Stretch enhancers emerge from smaller regions of active chromatin seeded at prior stages of development.
source: suggesting that SE emerge from smaller regions of active chromatin seeded at prior stages of development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that PSSE were classified as TE at earlier stages.

claim: During differentiation into mature islet cells, pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers lost H3K27ac but largely retained H3K4me1 signal (62% of PSSE).
source: During differentiation into mature islet cells, PSSE lost H3K27ac but largely retained H3K4me1 signal (62% of PSSE) (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers persist in a poised state in terminally differentiated islet cells.
source: persisting in a poised state in terminally differentiated islet cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the chromatin state analysis showing retention of H3K4me1 but loss of H3K27ac.

claim: Motifs associated with transcription factors FOXA, PDX1, GATA, ONECUT, and RBPJ were enriched in accessible chromatin sites within pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers.
source: Consistent with the activation of PSSE upon pancreas induction, motifs associated with transcription factors known to regulate pancreatic development (Conrad et al., 2014; Masui et al., 2007) were enriched, including FOXA (p=1 × 10−34), PDX1 (p=1 × 10−30), GATA (p=1 × 10−25), ONECUT (p=1 × 10−17), and RBPJ (p=1 × 10−14)
evidence: This is a finding from motif enrichment analysis with statistical significance values.

claim: Pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors activate pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers.
source: suggesting that pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors activate PSSE.
evidence: This is an inference based on the motif enrichment analysis and ChIP-seq overlap analysis.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers showed significant overlap with ChIP-seq binding sites for FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, PDX1, HNF6, and SOX9 at the PP2 stage (p<1 × 10−4 for all transcription factors).
source: Analysis of the extent of PSSE overlap with ChIP-seq binding sites for FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, PDX1, HNF6, and SOX9 at the PP2 stage substantiated this prediction (p<1 × 10−4 for all transcription factors; permutation test; Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from ChIP-seq overlap analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Predicted target genes for pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers showed enrichment for gene ontology terms related to tissue morphogenesis (p=1 × 10−7) and vascular development (p=1 × 10−8).
source: Annotation of biological functions of predicted target genes for PSSE (nearest gene with FPKM ≥1 at PP2 stage) revealed gene ontology terms related to developmental processes, such as tissue morphogenesis (p=1 × 10−7) and vascular development (p=1 × 10−8)
evidence: This is a finding from gene ontology analysis with statistical significance values.

claim: Predicted target genes for pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers showed enrichment for developmental signaling pathways, including BMP (p=1 × 10−5), NOTCH (p=1 × 10−4), and canonical Wnt signaling (p=1 × 10−4).
source: as well as developmental signaling pathways, including BMP (p=1 × 10−5), NOTCH (p=1 × 10−4), and canonical Wnt signaling (p=1 × 10−4; Figure 2E and Figure 2—source data 2)
evidence: This is a finding from gene ontology analysis with statistical significance values shown in Figure 2E.

claim: BMP, NOTCH, and canonical Wnt signaling pathways have demonstrated roles in pancreas morphogenesis and cell lineage allocation.
source: which have demonstrated roles in pancreas morphogenesis and cell lineage allocation (Ahnfelt-Rønne et al., 2010; Li et al., 2015; Murtaugh, 2008; Sharon et al., 2019; Sui et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: Transcript levels of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer-associated genes increased upon pancreatic lineage induction and peaked at the PP2 stage (p=1.8 × 10−8).
source: Consistent with the temporal pattern of H3K27ac deposition at PSSE, transcript levels of PSSE-associated genes increased upon pancreatic lineage induction and peaked at the PP2 stage (p=1.8 × 10−8; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Expression of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer-associated genes sharply decreased in islets (p<2.2 × 10−16).
source: Notably, expression of these genes sharply decreased in islets (p<2.2 × 10−16)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer-associated genes likely have a role in regulating pancreatic development but not mature islet function.
source: underscoring the likely role of these genes in regulating pancreatic development but not mature islet function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of PSSE-associated genes.

claim: Variants in accessible chromatin sites of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers genome-wide were enriched for T2D association (log enrichment = 2.85, 95% CI = <-20, 4.09).
source: Variants in accessible chromatin sites of PSSE genome-wide were enriched for T2D association (log enrichment = 2.85, 95% CI = <-20, 4.09).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from functional GWAS enrichment analysis.

claim: Enrichment of variants associated with fasting proinsulin levels, HOMA-B, and acute insulin response was observed within islet stretch enhancers (Z = 2.8, Z = 2.6, and Z = 2.2, respectively).
source: As expected based on prior observations (Parker et al., 2013; Pasquali et al., 2014), we observed enrichment (Z > 1.96) of variants associated with quantitative traits related to insulin secretion and beta cell function within islet SE, exemplified by fasting proinsulin levels, HOMA-B, and acute insulin response (Z = 2.8, Z = 2.6, and Z = 2.2, respectively; Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from LD score regression analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers showed a trend toward depletion for insulin secretion and beta cell function traits, although the estimates were not significant.
source: Conversely, PSSE showed a trend toward depletion for these traits, although the estimates were not significant.
evidence: This is a finding from LD score regression analysis.

claim: There was significant enrichment of beta cell trait association among islet stretch enhancer variants (χ2 test; p<0.05 for all beta cell functional traits except for insulin secretion rate).
source: There was significant enrichment of beta cell trait association among islet SE variants (χ2 test; p<0.05 for all beta cell functional traits except for insulin secretion rate), but no corresponding enrichment for PSSE (Figure 2—source data 3).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from chi-square test analysis shown in Figure 2—source data 3.

claim: There was no enrichment of beta cell trait association among pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer variants.
source: There was significant enrichment of beta cell trait association among islet SE variants (χ2 test; p<0.05 for all beta cell functional traits except for insulin secretion rate), but no corresponding enrichment for PSSE (Figure 2—source data 3).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from chi-square test analysis shown in Figure 2—source data 3.

claim: Variants at the LAMA1 locus had stronger effects on T2D risk among lean relative to obese cases.
source: A prior study found that variants at the LAMA1 locus had stronger effects on T2D risk among lean relative to obese cases (Perry et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Nominally significant enrichment of variants in pancreatic progenitor stretch enhancers for T2D among lean cases was observed (Z = 2.1).
source: We observed nominally significant enrichment of variants in pancreatic progenitor SE for T2D among lean cases (Z = 2.1).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from LD score regression analysis.

claim: Variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers were mildly enriched for T2D among lean (Z = 1.1) and depleted among obese (Z = −0.70) cases, although neither estimate was significant.
source: Variants in PSSE were mildly enriched for T2D among lean (Z = 1.1) and depleted among obese (Z = −0.70) cases, although neither estimate was significant.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from LD score regression analysis.

claim: Islet stretch enhancers showed positive enrichment for T2D among both lean (Z = 1.9) and obese cases (Z = 1.3).
source: By comparison, islet SE showed positive enrichment for T2D among both lean (Z = 1.9) and obese cases (Z = 1.3; Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from LD score regression analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers may affect T2D risk in a manner distinct from islet stretch enhancer function.
source: Together, these results suggest that PSSE may affect T2D risk in a manner distinct from islet SE function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential enrichment patterns observed.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers exhibited virtually no active chromatin during adipogenesis (9, 8, 6, and 8 out of the 492 PSSE were active enhancers in hACS-1, hASC-2, hASC-3, and hASC-4, respectively).
source: PSSE exhibited virtually no active chromatin during adipogenesis (9, 8, 6, and 8 out of the 492 PSSE were active enhancers in hACS-1, hASC-2, hASC-3, and hASC-4, respectively; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from chromatin state analysis during adipogenesis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are highly pancreatic progenitor-specific across T2D-relevant tissues and cell types.
source: These findings identify PSSE as highly pancreatic progenitor-specific across T2D-relevant tissues and cell types.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tissue specificity analysis.

claim: There were 49 variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers with T2D association exceeding p=4.7 × 10−6, mapping to 11 loci.
source: In total there were 49 variants in PSSE with T2D association exceeding this threshold mapping to 11 loci (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from variant mapping analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: T2D-associated variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers mapped to nine loci with known genome-wide significant T2D association (PROX1, ST6GAL1, SMARCAD1, XKR6, INS-IGF2, HMGA2, SMEK1, HMG20A, and LAMA1).
source: This included variants at nine loci with known genome-wide significant T2D association (PROX1, ST6GAL1, SMARCAD1, XKR6, INS-IGF2, HMGA2, SMEK1, HMG20A, and LAMA1)
evidence: This is a finding from variant mapping analysis.

claim: T2D-associated variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers mapped to two previously unreported loci with sub-genome-wide significant association, CRB2 and PGM1.
source: as well as at two previously unreported loci with sub-genome-wide significant association, CRB2 and PGM1.
evidence: This is a finding from variant mapping analysis identifying novel loci.

claim: Predicted target genes of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are similarly expressed in hESC-derived pancreatic progenitors and primary human embryonic pancreas.
source: Our finding that predicted target genes of PSSE are similarly expressed in hESC-derived pancreatic progenitors and primary human embryonic pancreas (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) further underscores the utility of the hESC-based system for these studies.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis comparing hESC-derived and primary tissue shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: None of the strongly T2D-associated variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers (p=4.7 × 10−6) overlapped an islet accessible chromatin site in T2D islets.
source: None of the strongly T2D-associated variants in PSSE (p=4.7 × 10−6) overlapped an islet accessible chromatin site in T2D islets
evidence: This is a finding from overlap analysis with T2D islet ATAC-seq data.

claim: T2D-associated variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are not relevant for broadly regulating islet gene activity during T2D.
source: arguing against the relevance of PSSE in broadly regulating islet gene activity during T2D.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of overlap with T2D islet accessible chromatin.

claim: Multiple T2D-associated variants mapped within the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer at genome-wide significance.
source: Variants in a PSSE at the LAMA1 locus were associated with T2D at genome-wide significance (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is a finding from GWAS analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: LAMA1 was highly expressed in the human embryonic pancreas.
source: and LAMA1 was highly expressed in the human embryonic pancreas (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The activity of the pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer at the LAMA1 locus was almost exclusively restricted to pancreatic progenitors.
source: Furthermore, the activity of the PSSE at the LAMA1 locus was almost exclusively restricted to pancreatic progenitors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C)
evidence: This is a finding from H3K27ac signal analysis across tissues shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer was among the most progenitor-specific across all pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers harboring T2D risk variants.
source: and was further among the most progenitor-specific across all PSSE harboring T2D risk variants (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from specificity analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Reporter gene assays in zebrafish embryos have shown that the LAMA1 enhancer drives gene expression specific to pancreatic progenitors in vivo.
source: In addition, reporter gene assays in zebrafish embryos have shown that this enhancer drives gene expression specific to pancreatic progenitors in vivo (Cebola et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Multiple T2D-associated variants mapped within the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer and were in the 99% credible set in fine-mapping data.
source: Multiple T2D-associated variants mapped within the LAMA1 PSSE, and these variants were further in the 99% credible set in fine-mapping data from the DIAMANTE consortium (Mahajan et al., 2018; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from fine-mapping analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: No other variants in the 99% credible set at the LAMA1 locus mapped in an accessible chromatin site active in islets from either non-diabetic or T2D samples.
source: No other variants in the 99% credible set mapped in an accessible chromatin site active in islets from either non-diabetic or T2D samples.
evidence: This is a finding from overlap analysis with islet ATAC-seq data.

claim: The LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer is intronic to the LAMA1 gene and contains regions of poised chromatin and typical enhancer at prior developmental stages.
source: The PSSE is intronic to the LAMA1 gene and contains regions of poised chromatin and TE at prior developmental stages (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from chromatin state analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Regions of open chromatin within the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer were already present at the DE and GT stages.
source: Consistent with its stepwise genesis as a SE throughout development, regions of open chromatin within the LAMA1 PSSE were already present at the DE and GT stages.
evidence: This is a finding from ATAC-seq analysis.

claim: Pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, HNF6, SOX9, and PDX1 were all bound to the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer at the PP2 stage.
source: Furthermore, pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors, such as FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, HNF6, SOX9, and PDX1, were all bound to the PSSE at the PP2 stage (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The T2D risk variant rs10502347 overlapped an ATAC-seq peak as well as ChIP-seq sites for multiple pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors.
source: Among credible set variants in the LAMA1 PSSE, rs10502347 overlapped an ATAC-seq peak as well as ChIP-seq sites for multiple pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors.
evidence: This is a finding from overlap analysis of variant position with ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: The T2D risk variant rs10502347 directly coincided with a SOX9 footprint identified in ATAC-seq data from PP2 cells.
source: Additionally, rs10502347 directly coincided with a SOX9 footprint identified in ATAC-seq data from PP2 cells
evidence: This is a finding from ATAC-seq footprinting analysis.

claim: The T2D risk allele C at rs10502347 is predicted to disrupt SOX9 binding.
source: and the T2D risk allele C is predicted to disrupt SOX9 binding (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a prediction based on footprinting analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The variant rs10502347 showed no association with beta cell function (p=0.81, 0.23, 0.46 for fasting proinsulin levels, HOMA-B, and acute insulin response, respectively).
source: Consistent with the collective endophenotype association patterns of PSSE (Figure 2F), rs10502347 showed no association with beta cell function (p=0.81, 0.23, 0.46 for fasting proinsulin levels, HOMA-B, and acute insulin response, respectively; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from GWAS association analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The T2D variant rs10502347 is predicted to affect the binding of pancreatic transcription factors and does not appear to affect beta cell function.
source: Thus, T2D variant rs10502347 is predicted to affect the binding of pancreatic transcription factors and does not appear to affect beta cell function.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the footprinting and association analyses.

claim: Two independent clonal hESC lines harboring homozygous deletions of the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer were generated.
source: To directly assess the function of the LAMA1 PSSE in regulating gene activity, we utilized CRIPSR-Cas9-mediated genome editing to generate two independent clonal human hESC lines harboring homozygous deletions of the LAMA1 PSSE (hereafter referred to as ∆LAMA1Enh; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: LAMA1 was expressed at similar levels in ∆LAMA1Enh and control cells at early developmental stages (ES, DE, GT, PP1).
source: LAMA1 was expressed at similar levels in ∆LAMA1Enh and control cells at early developmental stages, but was significantly reduced in PP2 cells derived from ∆LAMA1Enh clones (p=0.319, 0.594, 0.945, 0.290, and <1 × 10−6 for comparisons in ES, DE, GT, PP1, and PP2, respectively; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: LAMA1 expression was significantly reduced in PP2 cells derived from ∆LAMA1Enh clones (p<1 × 10−6).
source: LAMA1 was expressed at similar levels in ∆LAMA1Enh and control cells at early developmental stages, but was significantly reduced in PP2 cells derived from ∆LAMA1Enh clones (p=0.319, 0.594, 0.945, 0.290, and <1 × 10−6 for comparisons in ES, DE, GT, PP1, and PP2, respectively; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ARHGAP28 was the only other expressed gene within the topologically associated domain containing the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer.
source: ARHGAP28 was the only other expressed gene within the TAD
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq and Hi-C analysis.

claim: ARHGAP28 showed a trend toward lower expression in ∆LAMA1Enh PP2 cells, although not significantly different from controls (p.adj >0.05).
source: and albeit not significantly different from controls (p.adj >0.05), showed a trend toward lower expression in ∆LAMA1Enh PP2 cells (Figure 4E)
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ARHGAP28 may be an additional target gene of the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer.
source: raising the possibility that ARHGAP28 is an additional target gene of the LAMA1 PSSE.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the expression trend observed.

claim: While LAMA1 itself is broadly expressed across developmental stages, the T2D-associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer regulates LAMA1 expression specifically in pancreatic progenitors.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that while LAMA1 itself is broadly expressed across developmental stages, the T2D-associated PSSE regulates LAMA1 expression specifically in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the stage-specific effect of enhancer deletion on LAMA1 expression.

claim: ∆LAMA1Enh and control PP2 stage cultures contained similar percentages of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells.
source: At the PP2 stage, ∆LAMA1Enh and control cultures contained similar percentages of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells.
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry and immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: mRNA expression of PDX1, NKX6.1, PROX1, PTF1A, and SOX9 was either unaffected or only minimally reduced in ∆LAMA1Enh PP2 cells (p adj. = 3.56 × 10−2, 0.224, 0.829, 8.14 × 10−2, and 0.142, respectively).
source: Furthermore, mRNA expression of PDX1, NKX6.1, PROX1, PTF1A, and SOX9 was either unaffected or only minimally reduced (p adj. = 3.56 × 10−2, 0.224, 0.829, 8.14 × 10−2, and 0.142, for comparisons of PDX1, NKX6.1, PROX1, PTF1A, and SOX9 expression, respectively; Figure 4—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The overall gene expression profiles were similar in ∆LAMA1Enh and control PP2 cells.
source: and the overall gene expression profiles as determined by RNA-seq were similar in ∆LAMA1Enh and control PP2 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and Figure 4—source datas 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq correlation analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: ∆LAMA1 and control PP2 stage cultures contained similar numbers of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells.
source: Similar to ∆LAMA1Enh cultures, ∆LAMA1 and control PP2 stage cultures contained similar numbers of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: mRNA expression of PDX1, NKX6.1, PROX1, PTF1A, and SOX9 was similar in ∆LAMA1 and control PP2 cells (p=4.3 × 10−2, 0.19, 0.16, 0.17, and 8.7 × 10−2, respectively).
source: Likewise, mRNA expression of PDX1, NKX6.1, PROX1, PTF1A, and SOX9 was similar in ∆LAMA1 and control PP2 cells (p=4.3 × 10−2, 0.19, 0.16, 0.17, and 8.7 × 10−2, respectively; Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Neither deletion of the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer nor the LAMA1 gene overtly impairs pancreatic lineage induction in the in vitro hESC differentiation system.
source: These findings indicate that in vitro pancreatic lineage induction is unperturbed in both ∆LAMA1Enh cells exhibiting reduced LAMA1 expression, as well as ∆LAMA1 cells where LAMA1 coding sequences are disrupted.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the phenotypic characterization of deletion lines.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers harboring variants at CRB2 and PGM1 were intronic to their respective genes, contained ATAC-seq peaks, and bound pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, HNF6, SOX9, and PDX1.
source: As with the LAMA1 PSSE, PSSE harboring variants at CRB2 and PGM1 were intronic to their respective genes, contained ATAC-seq peaks, and bound pancreatic lineage-determining transcription factors FOXA1, FOXA2, GATA4, GATA6, HNF6, SOX9, and PDX1 (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from chromatin analysis shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: CRB2 and PGM1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers were less specific to pancreatic progenitors compared to the LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer and exhibited significant H3K27ac signal in several other tissues and cell types, most notably brain, liver, and the digestive tract.
source: Compared to the LAMA1 PSSE, CRB2 and PGM1 PSSE were less specific to pancreatic progenitors and exhibited significant H3K27ac signal in several other tissues and cell types, most notably brain, liver, and the digestive tract (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from H3K27ac signal analysis across tissues shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: CRB2 is a component of the Crumbs protein complex involved in the regulation of cell polarity and neuronal, heart, retinal, and kidney development.
source: CRB2 is a component of the Crumbs protein complex involved in the regulation of cell polarity and neuronal, heart, retinal, and kidney development (Alves et al., 2013; Bulgakova and Knust, 2009; Dudok et al., 2016; Jiménez-Amilburu and Stainier, 2019; Slavotinek et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: The role of CRB2 in pancreatic development is unknown.
source: However, its role in pancreatic development is unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the lack of prior knowledge.

claim: Two independent hESC clones with homozygous deletions of the CRB2 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer were generated.
source: To determine whether the CRB2 PSSE regulates CRB2 expression in pancreatic progenitors, we generated two independent hESC clones with homozygous deletions of the CRB2 PSSE (hereafter referred to as ∆CRB2Enh; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In control cells, CRB2 was first expressed at the GT stage and increased markedly at the PP1 stage.
source: In control cells, CRB2 was first expressed at the GT stage and increased markedly at the PP1 stage (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The pattern of CRB2 expression is consistent with H3K27ac deposition at the CRB2 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer in GT stage cells and classification as a stretch enhancer at the PP1 and PP2 stages.
source: This pattern of CRB2 expression is consistent with H3K27ac deposition at the CRB2 PSSE in GT stage cells and classification as a SE at the PP1 and PP2 stages (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between expression and chromatin state.

claim: In ∆CRB2Enh cells, upregulation of CRB2 expression was observed at earlier developmental stages, in particular at the DE and GT stages (p<1 × 10−6 at both stages).
source: In ∆CRB2Enh cells, we observed upregulation of CRB2 expression at earlier developmental stages, in particular at the DE and GT stages (p<1 × 10−6 at both stages; Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The CRB2 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer may be associated with repressive transcriptional complexes prior to pancreas induction.
source: suggesting that the CRB2 PSSE may be associated with repressive transcriptional complexes prior to pancreas induction.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the upregulation of CRB2 in early stages upon enhancer deletion.

claim: At the PP2 stage, CRB2 expression was significantly reduced in ∆CRB2Enh cells (p adj. = 3.51 × 10−3).
source: At the PP2 stage, CRB2 expression was significantly reduced in ∆CRB2Enh cells (p adj. = 3.51 × 10−3; Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from qPCR analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The expression of other genes in the same topologically associated domain as CRB2 was not affected in ∆CRB2Enh cells (p adj. ≥0.05).
source: whereas the expression of other genes in the same TAD was not affected (p adj. ≥0.05; Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The CRB2 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer specifically regulates CRB2 and is required for CRB2 expression in pancreatic progenitors.
source: Thus, the CRB2 PSSE specifically regulates CRB2 and is required for CRB2 expression in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the stage-specific effect of enhancer deletion on CRB2 expression.

claim: ∆CRB2Enh and control PP2 stage cultures contained similar percentages of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells.
source: Phenotypic characterization of PP2 stage ∆CRB2Enh cultures revealed similar percentages of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells as in control cultures (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: The expression of pancreatic transcription factors and global gene expression profiles were similar in ∆CRB2Enh and control PP2 cells.
source: The expression of pancreatic transcription factors and global gene expression profiles were also similar in ∆CRB2Enh and control PP2 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D,E and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D,E.

claim: CRB2 deletion hESCs differentiated to the PP2 stage produced similar numbers of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells as control cells.
source: Likewise, CRB2 deletion hESCs (∆CRB2) differentiated to the PP2 stage (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A,B) produced similar numbers of PDX1- and NKX6.1-positive cells and expressed pancreatic transcription factors at levels similar to control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–E).
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry and immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–E.

claim: Neither deletion of the CRB2 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer nor the CRB2 gene overtly impairs pancreatic lineage induction in the in vitro hESC differentiation system.
source: Thus, neither deletion of the CRB2 PSSE nor the CRB2 gene overtly impairs pancreatic lineage induction in the in vitro hESC differentiation system.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the phenotypic characterization of deletion lines.

claim: Laminin (encoded by LAMA1) and CRB2 are predicted to regulate processes related to tissue morphogenesis, such as cell migration, tissue growth, and cell allocation within the developing organ.
source: Based on their classification as extracellular matrix and cell polarity proteins, respectively, Laminin (encoded by LAMA1) and CRB2 are predicted to regulate processes related to tissue morphogenesis, such as cell migration, tissue growth, and cell allocation within the developing organ.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the known functions of these protein classes.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers in general were enriched for proximity to genes involved in tissue morphogenesis.
source: Furthermore, PSSE in general were enriched for proximity to genes involved in tissue morphogenesis (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a finding from gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: T2D risk variants acting within pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers could have roles in pancreas morphogenesis.
source: suggesting that T2D risk variants acting within PSSE could have roles in pancreas morphogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene ontology enrichment.

claim: Cell migratory processes and niche-specific signaling events are not fully modeled during hESC differentiation.
source: Since cell migratory processes and niche-specific signaling events are not fully modeled during hESC differentiation, we reasoned that the in vitro pancreatic differentiation system might not be suitable for studying Laminin and CRB2 function in pancreatic development.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the hESC differentiation system.

claim: The basic organization and cell types in the pancreas as well as the genes regulating endocrine and exocrine pancreas development are highly conserved between zebrafish and mammals.
source: The basic organization and cell types in the pancreas as well as the genes regulating endocrine and exocrine pancreas development are highly conserved between zebrafish and mammals (Dong et al., 2008; Field et al., 2003; Kimmel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: At 48 hr post-fertilization, both Laminin and Crb proteins were detected in the eGFP and Nkx6.1 co-positive pancreatic progenitor cell domain in zebrafish.
source: At 48 hr post-fertilization (hpf), both Laminin and Crb proteins were detected in the eGFP and Nkx6.1 co-positive pancreatic progenitor cell domain (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from immunohistochemistry analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Significant reduction of Laminin staining was observed throughout the pancreatic progenitor cell domain in embryos treated with morpholinos targeting lama1.
source: We observed significant reduction of Laminin staining throughout the pancreatic progenitor cell domain in embryos treated with morpholinos targeting lama1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is a finding from immunohistochemistry validation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: In embryos treated with morpholinos targeting crb2a or crb2a and crb2b, loss of staining was observed in the pancreatic progenitor cell domain using antibodies specific to Crb2a or antibodies detecting all Crb proteins, respectively.
source: In embryos treated with morpholinos targeting crb2a or crb2a and crb2b, we observed loss of staining in the pancreatic progenitor cell domain using antibodies specific to Crb2a or antibodies detecting all Crb proteins, respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–H)
evidence: This is a finding from immunohistochemistry validation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–H.

claim: lama1 morphants exhibited reduced body size and other gross anatomical defects at 78 hpf.
source: Consistent with prior studies (Pollard et al., 2006), lama1 morphants exhibited reduced body size and other gross anatomical defects at 78 hpf
evidence: This is a finding from zebrafish morphant analysis consistent with prior studies.

claim: crb2a/b morphants appeared grossly normal.
source: whereas crb2a/b morphants appeared grossly normal.
evidence: This is a finding from zebrafish morphant analysis.

claim: Both lama1 and crb2a/b morphants displayed an annular pancreas (15 out of 34 lama1 and 27 out of 69 crb2a/b morphants).
source: Both lama1 and crb2a/b morphants displayed an annular pancreas (15 out of 34 lama1 and 27 out of 69 crb2a/b morphants) characterized by pancreatic tissue partially or completely encircling the duodenum (Figure 6A–D)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from zebrafish morphant analysis shown in Figure 6A–D.

claim: An annular pancreas is a phenotype indicative of impaired migration of pancreatic progenitors during pancreas formation.
source: a phenotype indicative of impaired migration of pancreatic progenitors during pancreas formation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the annular pancreas phenotype based on developmental biology knowledge.

claim: Both lama1 and crb2a/b control cell migratory processes during early pancreatic development.
source: These findings suggest that both lama1 and crb2a/b control cell migratory processes during early pancreatic development
evidence: This is an inference based on the annular pancreas phenotype.

claim: Reduced levels of lama1 or crb2a/b impair pancreas morphogenesis.
source: and that reduced levels of lama1 or crb2a/b impair pancreas morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the morphant phenotypes.

claim: Beta cell numbers were significantly reduced in both lama1 and crb2a/b morphants (p=8.0 × 10−3 and 4.0 × 10−3, respectively).
source: Beta cell numbers were significantly reduced in both lama1 and crb2a/b morphants (p=8.0 × 10−3 and 4.0 × 10−3 for comparisons of lama1 and crb2a/b morphants, respectively; Figure 6E,F)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from beta cell quantification shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: Beta cell numbers were significantly reduced in morphants with a combined knockdown of lama1 and crb2a/b (p=2.0 × 10−4).
source: as well as in morphants with a combined knockdown of lama1 and crb2a/b (p=2.0 × 10−4; Figure 6F)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from beta cell quantification shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Reduced lama1 and crb2a/b levels, both individually and in combination, impair beta cell development.
source: showing that reduced lama1 and crb2a/b levels, both individually and in combination, impair beta cell development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the beta cell quantification results.

claim: Nearly all lama1, crb2a/b, and combined lama1 and crb2a/b morphants without an annular pancreas had reduced beta cell numbers.
source: Furthermore, we found that nearly all lama1, crb2a/b, and combined lama1 and crb2a/b morphants without an annular pancreas had reduced beta cell numbers
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of morphants without annular pancreas.

claim: lama1 and crb2 have independent roles in pancreas morphogenesis and beta cell differentiation.
source: indicating independent roles of lama1 and crb2 in pancreas morphogenesis and beta cell differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that beta cell defects occur independently of annular pancreas.

claim: Only crb2b morphants showed a significant reduction in beta cell numbers (p=4.4 × 10−2).
source: Only crb2b morphants showed a significant reduction in beta cell numbers (p=4.4 × 10−2; Figure 6—figure supplement 4)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from beta cell quantification shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: crb2b is the predominant crb2 gene required for beta cell development.
source: suggesting that crb2b is the predominant crb2 gene required for beta cell development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of crb2a and crb2b knockdown.

claim: lama1 and crb2 are regulators of pancreas morphogenesis and beta cell development in vivo.
source: Combined, these findings demonstrate that lama1 and crb2 are regulators of pancreas morphogenesis and beta cell development in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the zebrafish morphant phenotypes.

claim: T2D-associated variants localized within chromatin active in pancreatic progenitors but not islets or other T2D-relevant tissues were identified.
source: In this study, we identify T2D-associated variants localized within chromatin active in pancreatic progenitors but not islets or other T2D-relevant tissues
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claim: A subset of T2D risk variants specifically alters pancreatic developmental processes.
source: suggesting a novel mechanism whereby a subset of T2D risk variants specifically alters pancreatic developmental processes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment and functional studies.

claim: T2D-associated enhancers active in pancreatic progenitors were linked to the regulation of LAMA1 and CRB2.
source: We link T2D-associated enhancers active in pancreatic progenitors to the regulation of LAMA1 and CRB2
evidence: This is a summary of the enhancer deletion experiments.

claim: There is a functional requirement for lama1 and crb2 in pancreas morphogenesis and endocrine cell formation.
source: and demonstrate a functional requirement in zebrafish for lama1 and crb2 in pancreas morphogenesis and endocrine cell formation.
evidence: This is a summary of the zebrafish morphant experiments.

claim: A curated list of T2D risk-associated enhancers and candidate effector genes is provided for further exploration of how the regulation of developmental processes in the pancreas can predispose to T2D.
source: Furthermore, we provide a curated list of T2D risk-associated enhancers and candidate effector genes for further exploration of how the regulation of developmental processes in the pancreas can predispose to T2D.
evidence: This is a statement about the resource provided by the study.

claim: 11 loci were identified where T2D-associated variants mapped in stretch enhancers specifically active in pancreatic progenitors.
source: Our analysis identified 11 loci where T2D-associated variants mapped in SE specifically active in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary of the variant mapping analysis.

claim: Among the 11 loci with T2D-associated variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers was LAMA1, which has stronger effects on T2D risk in lean compared to obese individuals.
source: Among these loci was LAMA1, which has stronger effects on T2D risk in lean compared to obese individuals (Perry et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Variants in pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers collectively have stronger enrichment for T2D in lean individuals, although the small number of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers and limited sample size of the BMI-stratified T2D genetic data prohibits a more robust comparison.
source: We also found evidence that variants in PSSE collectively have stronger enrichment for T2D in lean individuals, although the small number of PSSE and limited sample size of the BMI-stratified T2D genetic data prohibits a more robust comparison.
evidence: This is a finding from the BMI-stratified analysis with caveats about statistical power.

claim: There was a notable lack of enrichment among pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer variants for association with traits related to insulin secretion and beta cell function.
source: There was also a notable lack of enrichment among PSSE variants for association with traits related to insulin secretion and beta cell function.
evidence: This is a finding from the endophenotype enrichment analysis.

claim: Variants affecting beta cell developmental processes may have no overt phenotypic effect under physiological conditions and contribute to T2D pathogenesis only during the disease process.
source: As genetic association studies of endophenotypes are based on data from non-diabetic subjects, a possible explanation is that variants affecting beta cell developmental processes have no overt phenotypic effect under physiological conditions and contribute to T2D pathogenesis only during the disease process.
evidence: This is a speculation to explain the lack of endophenotype enrichment.

claim: The genomic position of enhancers and transcription factor binding sites is not well conserved between species.
source: Since the genomic position of enhancers and transcription factor binding sites is not well conserved between species (Villar et al., 2015)
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: A human cell model is necessary to identify target genes of enhancers associated with disease risk.
source: a human cell model is necessary to identify target genes of enhancers associated with disease risk.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of enhancer conservation.

claim: T2D-associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers at the LAMA1 and CRB2 loci regulate LAMA1 and CRB2, respectively, and establish LAMA1 and CRB2 as the predominant target gene of their corresponding pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer within TAD boundaries.
source: By employing enhancer deletion in hESCs, we demonstrate that T2D-associated PSSE at the LAMA1 and CRB2 loci regulate LAMA1 and CRB2, respectively, and establish LAMA1 and CRB2 as the predominant target gene of their corresponding PSSE within TAD boundaries.
evidence: This is a summary of the enhancer deletion experiments.

claim: The identified pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers control LAMA1 and CRB2 expression in a temporal manner consistent with the activation pattern of their associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers.
source: By analyzing LAMA1 and CRB2 expression throughout the pancreatic differentiation time course, we show that the identified PSSE control LAMA1 and CRB2 expression in a temporal manner consistent with the activation pattern of their associated PSSE.
evidence: This is a finding from the expression analysis across differentiation stages.

claim: Several T2D-associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are localized within TADs containing genes encoding transcriptional regulators, including PROX1 and GATA4.
source: it is notable that several are localized within TADs containing genes encoding transcriptional regulators. These include PROX1 and GATA4, which are known to regulate pancreatic development (Shi et al., 2017; Tiyaboonchai et al., 2017; Westmoreland et al., 2012)
evidence: This is an observation from the TAD analysis with cited knowledge about gene function.

claim: PROX1 and GATA4 are known to regulate pancreatic development.
source: These include PROX1 and GATA4, which are known to regulate pancreatic development (Shi et al., 2017; Tiyaboonchai et al., 2017; Westmoreland et al., 2012)
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: Several T2D-associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are localized within TADs containing genes encoding HMGA2 and BCL6 with unknown functions in the pancreas.
source: as well as HMGA2 and BCL6 with unknown functions in the pancreas.
evidence: This is an observation from the TAD analysis with a statement about lack of knowledge.

claim: The catalogue of T2D-associated pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers provides a resource to fully characterize the gene regulatory program associated with developmentally mediated T2D risk in the pancreas.
source: Our catalogue of T2D-associated PSSE provides a resource to fully characterize the gene regulatory program associated with developmentally mediated T2D risk in the pancreas.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the resource provided.

claim: Predicted target genes of pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancers are similarly expressed in hESC-derived pancreatic progenitors and primary human embryonic pancreas, underscoring the utility of the hESC-based system for these studies.
source: Our finding that predicted target genes of PSSE are similarly expressed in hESC-derived pancreatic progenitors and primary human embryonic pancreas (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) further underscores the utility of the hESC-based system for these studies.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of expression in hESC-derived and primary tissue.

claim: In the embryo, endocrine cells differentiate by delaminating from a polarized epithelium of progenitors governed by local cell-cell and cell-matrix signaling events.
source: In the embryo, endocrine cells differentiate by delaminating from a polarized epithelium of progenitors governed by local cell-cell and cell-matrix signaling events (Mamidi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Cell-cell and cell-matrix signaling processes are not well-recapitulated in the hESC-based pancreatic differentiation system.
source: These processes are not well-recapitulated in the hESC-based pancreatic differentiation system
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the hESC system.

claim: The hESC-based pancreatic differentiation system has limitations for studying the function of Laminin and CRB2, which are mediators of mechanical signals within an epithelium.
source: highlighting a limitation of this system for studying the function of Laminin and CRB2, which are mediators of mechanical signals within an epithelium.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the hESC system for studying these specific proteins.

claim: lama1 or crb2 knockdown leads to an annular pancreas and reduced beta cell numbers in zebrafish.
source: We show that lama1 or crb2 knockdown leads to an annular pancreas and reduced beta cell numbers.
evidence: This is a summary of the zebrafish morphant phenotypes.

claim: The beta cell differentiation defect was evident in zebrafish embryos not displaying an annular pancreas, suggesting independent mechanisms.
source: The beta cell differentiation defect was also evident in embryos not displaying an annular pancreas, suggesting independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of morphants without annular pancreas.

claim: Culture of pancreatic progenitors on Laminin-based substrates promotes endocrine cell differentiation.
source: Consistent with our findings in lama1 morphants, culture of pancreatic progenitors on Laminin-based substrates promotes endocrine cell differentiation (Mamidi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study that is consistent with the findings.

claim: During in vivo pancreatic development, endothelial cells are an important albeit not the only source of Laminin in the pancreas.
source: During in vivo pancreatic development, endothelial cells are an important albeit not the only source of Laminin in the pancreas (Heymans et al., 2019; Mamidi et al., 2018; Nikolova et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: The T2D-associated LAMA1 pancreatic progenitor-specific stretch enhancer is not active in endothelial cells.
source: the T2D-associated LAMA1 PSSE is not active in endothelial cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from H3K27ac signal analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: No other T2D-associated variants at the LAMA1 locus map in endothelial cell enhancers or accessible chromatin sites in islets.
source: Furthermore, we found no other T2D-associated variants at the LAMA1 locus mapping in endothelial cell enhancers or accessible chromatin sites in islets
evidence: This is a finding from variant mapping analysis.

claim: T2D risk at the LAMA1 locus is linked to LAMA1 regulation in pancreatic progenitors.
source: suggesting that T2D risk is linked to LAMA1 regulation in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the tissue specificity of the LAMA1 PSSE and variant mapping.

claim: CRB2 has been shown to regulate mechanosignaling.
source: Similar to Laminin, CRB2 has been shown to regulate mechanosignaling (Varelas et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Pancreatic progenitor cells express Crb proteins.
source: Our observation that pancreatic progenitor cells express Crb proteins is consistent with the phenotype of crb2 morphants reflecting a progenitor-autonomous role of Crb2.
evidence: This is a finding from immunohistochemistry analysis.

claim: The phenotype of crb2 morphants reflects a progenitor-autonomous role of Crb2.
source: Our observation that pancreatic progenitor cells express Crb proteins is consistent with the phenotype of crb2 morphants reflecting a progenitor-autonomous role of Crb2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern and morphant phenotype.

claim: The similarity in pancreatic phenotype between lama1 or crb2 morphants raises the possibility that signals from Laminin and Crb2 could converge on the same intracellular pathways in pancreatic progenitors.
source: Furthermore, the similarity in pancreatic phenotype between lama1 or crb2 morphants raises the possibility that signals from Laminin and Crb2 could converge on the same intracellular pathways in pancreatic progenitors.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the similar phenotypes.

claim: Variation in gene regulation during pancreatic development can predispose to T2D later in life.
source: Our findings suggest that variation in gene regulation during pancreatic development can predispose to T2D later in life.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Human genetic studies have shown a strong correlation between birth weight and adult cardiometabolic traits and disease.
source: First, human genetic studies have shown a strong correlation between birth weight and adult cardiometabolic traits and disease (Horikoshi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Epidemiological studies provide evidence that offspring of mothers who were pregnant during a famine have a higher prevalence of T2D.
source: Second, epidemiological studies provide evidence that offspring of mothers who were pregnant during a famine have a higher prevalence of T2D (Lumey et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Maternal malnutrition has been shown to cause reduced beta cell mass at birth and to render beta cells more prone to failure under stress in rodents.
source: This phenomenon has been experimentally reproduced in rodents, where maternal malnutrition has been shown to cause reduced beta cell mass at birth and to render beta cells more prone to failure under stress (Nielsen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The results provide a strong rationale for further exploration of how genetic variants affecting developmental gene regulation in the pancreas contribute to T2D risk.
source: Together, our results provide a strong rationale for further exploration of how genetic variants affecting developmental gene regulation in the pancreas contribute to T2D risk.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the implications of the study.
